meta.name: Write safe procedures from screen recordings with Google Gemini

name: Write a procedure from a screen recording, re-watching anything it could not read

parameters.formTitle: Turn a screen recording into a written procedure

values.placeholder: e.g. Issuing a refund in the billing system
e.g. New support agents in their first week

parameters.formDescription: Record yourself doing the task once. Anything the recording does not show clearly is re-watched rather than guessed at.

parameters.text:
=You are watching a screen recording of someone performing "{{ $json.processName }}". Write it up as a procedure, and be honest about what you could not make out.

Reply with ONLY minified JSON, no prose and no code fences:
{"steps":[{"t":"seconds as a number","do":"the action in the imperative","where":"the app, screen or menu path visible","watch":"anything easy to get wrong, or empty string","sure":true,"ask":"if sure is false, the precise question to answer on a second viewing"}],"tools_used":["app names seen"],"outcome":"what the process achieves","recording_quality":"clear|partly unclear|unusable","quality_note":"what made it hard to follow, or empty string"}

Set sure to false whenever you are inferring rather than reading - a field name you could not quite make out, a click whose target was off screen or covered by a cursor, a value typed too fast to read, a menu that opened and closed in a blur. Do not quietly guess and mark it true. When sure is false, write ask as a specific question about that moment, such as "What exact value was typed into the Reason field at 00:47?".

Use the words that actually appear on screen. Do not invent steps you did not see. If the recording shows nothing recognisable, set recording_quality to unusable and return an empty steps array.

nodes.name: Judge if It Is Safe to Follow

parameters.text:
=Steps were read off a screen recording of "{{ $json.processName }}", and {{ $json.recheckedCount }} unclear moment(s) were re-watched - {{ $json.verifiedCount }} resolved, {{ $json.stillUnclearCount }} still unreadable. You have to hand this to {{ $json.audience }} and be confident they will not get stuck. It is rated {{ $json.criticality }}.

Apps seen: {{ $json.toolsUsed }}
Outcome: {{ $json.outcome }}
Recording quality: {{ $json.recordingQuality }} {{ $json.quality_note }}
Steps ({{ $json.stepCount }}):
{{ $json.stepsText }}

A recording only ever shows the happy path performed by someone who already knows how. Name what it did NOT show.

- missing_prerequisites: access, permissions, data or approvals the recorder already had and never demonstrated obtaining.
- undemonstrated_failures: the realistic ways this goes wrong that never appeared - errors, rejections, missing records, timeouts.
- tacit_knowledge: moments where the recorder made a judgement a newcomer could not make from the screen alone.
- risky_steps: anything irreversible, customer-visible or costly, and why.
- completeness_score: 0-100 for how safely {{ $json.audience }} could follow this unaided. Fewer than four steps, or an unusable recording, must score below 40. Any step still marked unclear after re-watching caps the score at 60. A Business critical process with undemonstrated failure paths cannot exceed 74.
- quiz: three to five short questions with answers that check understanding, not reading.

Be specific to this process. Never write generic advice like "follow company policy". Return an empty array where a category genuinely has nothing.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: {"completeness_score":72,"verdict":"A usable draft, but three things were never shown on screen","missing_prerequisites":["Which permission level is needed to see the Billing tab"],"undemonstrated_failures":["What to do when the refund is declined"],"tacit_knowledge":["The recorder knew which of two customer records was correct without checking"],"risky_steps":["Step 6 is irreversible once confirmed"],"quiz":[{"question":"What must you check before confirming?","answer":"That the order ID matches the complaint"}]}

parameters.content:
## Write a procedure from a screen recording, re-watching anything it could not read

### Why this exists
Every team has processes that live in one person head. Writing them down takes an hour nobody has, so it never happens - and then that person goes on holiday.

Recording yourself doing the task takes two minutes. The problem with turning that into a document is that a model asked to describe a video will describe all of it confidently, including the field it could not actually read. A procedure with one wrong value in it is worse than no procedure, because someone will follow it.

### How it works
This template does not take the first answer. Gemini watches the recording once and, for every step, must declare whether it read the screen or inferred it - a value typed too fast, a click behind the cursor, a menu that blurred past. Where it is unsure it must write the precise question it would need answered.

Those uncertain moments, and only those, are then fed one at a time back into the same video with a targeted question about that timestamp. Looking once at a whole recording and looking again at one second of it are very different tasks, and the second usually succeeds. Anything still unreadable after the second viewing is written into the procedure as unreadable rather than quietly filled in.

Only then is the draft judged. A separate chain names what the recording never showed at all - the permissions the recorder already had, the failure paths that never came up, the judgement calls invisible on screen, the irreversible steps - and scores how safely the stated audience could follow it. Any step still unclear caps that score.

The score decides the outcome. Below 40 there is no document, only a page saying exactly what to record again. Between 40 and 74 the workbook carries a VERIFY BEFORE USE section. Above 74 it comes through clean. The Excel file downloads straight from the browser and every row is marked: shown on the recording, confirmed on a second viewing, or unreadable.

### Floating nodes - wire in what you need
Three optional nodes sit unconnected at the bottom of the canvas. Drag a connection from Make the Workbook to any of them to announce new procedures in Slack, keep a master register in Google Sheets, or email the process owner. Delete the ones you do not want.

### Setup
1. Connect Google Gemini (PaLM) API. That is the only credential the main path needs.
2. Open Upload the Recording and copy the production form URL.
3. Optional: connect Slack, Sheets or Gmail only if you wire in a floating node.

### Customization tips
Raise or lower MAX_RECHECKS in Find the Weak Points - it caps how many moments are re-watched so a poor recording cannot spiral into cost. Adjust the score thresholds in Route by Completeness, or add your own columns in the row builders.

## 1. Take the recording, and refuse a bad one
The file is checked before a single token is spent: wrong type, too short to contain a process, or too large stops here with a plain explanation of what to record instead.

## 2. Watch once - and admit what you could not read
Gemini writes up each action with its timestamp and the screen it happened on, but must also declare, per step, whether it read the screen or inferred it. Where it is unsure it writes the exact question it would need answered. That admission is what the rest of the workflow is built on.

## 3. Go back to the video, one moment at a time
Only the uncertain moments loop back into the same recording, each with a targeted question about its timestamp. Looking at a whole video and looking again at one second of it are different tasks, and the second usually succeeds. Anything still unreadable is recorded as unreadable, never guessed. The count is capped so a poor recording cannot spiral.

## 4. Judge it, then decide what you get
A separate chain names what the recording never showed at all and scores how safely the audience could follow it - and any step still unclear caps that score. Below 40 there is no document, just what to re-record. Between 40 and 74 the workbook carries a VERIFY BEFORE USE section. Above 74 it comes through clean.

## Floating nodes - optional, not connected
These three are deliberately left unconnected. Drag a connection from **Make the Workbook** into whichever you want, and delete the rest.

- **Announce It in Slack** - tell the team a new procedure exists.
- **Append to a Master Procedure Sheet** - keep a register of every process documented, with its confidence score, so you can see what still needs verifying.
- **Email It to the Owner** - send the steps to whoever owns the process for sign-off.

Each needs its own credential, which is why they are off by default - the main path runs on the Gemini credential alone.
